title: Async Telemetry Bridge with Ordered Replay
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Implement a lightweight async telemetry bridge in the SDK and edge middleware that preserves causal ordering across unreliable transports and supports ordered replay when the outbound telemetry pipeline temporarily drops or backpressures. This ticket covers SDK hooks, middleware adapters, a durable enqueue-and-replay flow, and dashboarding/alerts for telemetry reordering and replay health.

Background: We currently drop or silently re-order spans when network blips or our batching pipeline falls behind, which skews trace timelines and increases investigation time. The bridge should: 1) add minimal runtime overhead for hot paths; 2) be interoperable with existing OpenTelemetry headers and Redwood request envelope headers; 3) provide best-effort ordering guarantees and idempotent replay; 4) expose metrics and logs to monitor replay/ordering behavior.

Non-goals: Building a full durable queueing service (we will reuse existing local disk queue + cloud ingestion). This work focuses on SDK/middleware semantics and primitives that let the runtime and ingestion pipeline recover traces with ordering.

Acceptance criteria:
- SDK exposes an optional lightweight "telemetry bridge" that attaches a monotonic sequence and transaction ID to each root/span so replay can be ordered.
- Middleware translates existing tracing headers and emits the bridge envelope when enabled via feature flag.
- When outbound ingestion responds with 429 or transient TCP failures, spans are enqueued to local bounded storage and replayed in-order with exponential backoff and jitter.
- Replay is idempotent (sequence+txid) and deduplicated by ingestion service when seen twice.
- Metrics emitted: telemetry_bridge_enqueue_count, telemetry_bridge_replay_count, telemetry_bridge_drop_count, telemetry_bridge_replay_lag_ms, telemetry_bridge_reordering_rate.
- New dashboards: Telemetry Bridge Health (per-region, per-service) and Trace Ordering Error table.
- End-to-end tests in staging demonstrating no more than 0.1% increase in tail latency and no >1% trace reordering under simulated network failures.

Design notes / trade-offs:
- Sequence vs. vector clocks: we chose per-transaction monotonic sequence numbers instead of full vector clocks to keep SDK overhead minimal and compatible with cross-service flows. This sacrifices perfect causal reconstruction for simplicity and performance.
- Durable store: use existing local bounded disk queue implementation (localfile-queue v2) to avoid introducing a new dependency. We add per-process size limit and LRU eviction policy to protect memory.
- Ordering guarantee is best-effort: if a downstream service permanently drops spans, order cannot be reconstructed; we will surface drop_count metrics and provide optional auto-fallback to sampling-based reconstruction.
- Idempotence: rely on ingestion-side dedupe using txid+seq. We coordinated the ingestion schema change in GH PR referenced below.
- Feature flag: default off. Controlled rollout by service and region.

API/SDK changes:
- New opt-in constructor parameter: telemetryBridge: { enabled: boolean, maxLocalQueueMb: integer, maxRecordAgeMs: integer }
- Middleware will add headers: X-RW-TXID, X-RW-SEQ, and keep existing OTel headers (traceparent, baggage).
- Backcompat: if telemetryBridge disabled, behavior is identical to current SDK.

Testing and rollout plan:
- Unit tests for sequence assignment, enqueue/replay logic, dedupe.
- Staging integration test: simulate ingestion 429s and TCP resets while generating 100k traces; validate ordering metrics and replay behavior.
- Canary rollout to 10% of services, monitor new dashboard and e2e trace correctness for 72 hours, then increase to 50% and 100%.
- Rollback plan: flip feature flag off to stop adding envelopes and drain local queues; ingest dedupe handles any duplicates.

Observability and alerts:
- Dashboards: Telemetry Bridge Health (per-service heatmap), Replay Lag distribution, Reordering Rate timeseries.
- Alerts: telemetry_bridge_drop_count > 0.5% of inbound spans for 5m -> P1; telemetry_bridge_replay_lag_ms p95 > 5s for 10m -> Pager.
- Logs: structured events for enqueue/replay/drop with txid, seq, span_id, service, region.

Storage and retention:
- Local queue items TTL default 300000ms (5m), configurable per-service. Items older than TTL are counted against telemetry_bridge_drop_count and evicted.

Dependencies:
- ingestion service schema change GH-PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingestion/pull/487
- localfile-queue v2 update: https://github.com/redwood-inference/localfile-queue/compare/v1...v2 (branch: durable-queue)
comments: 2026-02-25 - Aisha Patel: Created initial ticket after SRE incident where 18% of traces showed apparent parent-child reordering during a 15min outage. Attached incident summary and preliminary design notes to Confluence.

2026-03-01 - Marcus Reyes: Spent 2 days prototyping sequence assignment in JS/Go SDKs. Prototype adds ~120ns median overhead to hot path in JS (measured in microbench). Uploaded prototype notes: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/OBS/Async+Telemetry+Bridge+Prototype

2026-03-03 - Design review with Jules Kim (PM) and Elena Novak (SRE). Decision: per-transaction monotonic sequence + txid. PM requested clearer rollout gates and dashboards; SRE requested strict metrics for replay_lag and drop_count. Added to acceptance criteria.

2026-03-05 - Code review: GH PR opened for SDK changes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/762. Early feedback from reviewer Ben Chu: please add unit tests for cross-process replay ordering (simulated multi-worker flush).

2026-03-07 - Marcus Reyes: Implemented dedupe marker and added ingestion PR link. Run staging tests with simulated 429s: enqueue_count=12k, replay_count=11.9k, drop_count=100 (0.83%). We need to tune eviction TTL and queue size for python services in edge region eu-west-1.

2026-03-09 - QA (Priya Shah): Found a regression where SDK on process restart lost queued items if process crashed during flush. Mitigation: write-ahead pointer flush and atomic rename for durability. Marcus will land fix and re-run tests.

2026-03-10 - Marcus Reyes: Fixed atomic write issue, re-ran staging test. Results: drop_count=18 (0.15%), replay_lag_ms p95=3200ms, median increase in tail latency +0.08%. Ready for canary when ingestion dedupe deploys next week. Leaving for engineering ops to schedule canary rollout.
